title: bench_repro.match_facts pairs no paraphrase of one fact, so duplicate research and dup_facts miss differently worded duplicates
goal: match_facts pairs two facts on one article citing one source that state the same thing in other words, and still pairs no two different facts on that article

run:
import sys;sys.path.insert(0,'_tools');import bench_repro as R
f=lambda t:{'path':'public/x/y.md','text':t+' [DOC S-aaaa]','at':1.0,'ids':['S-aaaa'],'doc':['S-aaaa']}
m=R.match_facts([f('The export job sends 512 records in each request and retries a failed batch three times.')],[f('Each export request carries up to 512 records; a failed batch is retried three times.')])
print(m);sys.exit(0 if m else 1)

import sys;sys.path.insert(0,'_tools');import bench_repro as R

gates.question: How does match_facts pair two worded-differently facts that cite one source?
options: Raw words with TOKEN_OVERLAP lowered to 0.45
gates.reason: filler dropped and plural or verb endings cut, so a paraphrase pairs without loosening the cut for unrelated facts

notes: Planning 2026-10-27: goal narrowed to what the repro and the negative check read; found by the SP-n7f53pgv review (S2 on ST-f5lbn3aw). The matcher feeds the repro benchmark too, so a looser match changes its figures.
